claim: A published active-learning framework selected interventions to reduce uncertainty in causal models, providing an external computational precedent for choosing informative perturbations rather than screening every intervention uniformly.
future_grounding_route: A project-specific pilot must compare a frozen active or optimal design with a random-design control on held-out perturbations; model-selected interventions remain proposals until experimentally measured.
project_use: External design context only; the project separately tests a generic D-optimal pair design on seeded synthetic screens.
relationship_note: The source motivates intervention selection, while the project's synthetic probe establishes only assumption-conditional method behavior and no biology.

source.citation: Active learning for optimal intervention design in causal models. Nature Machine Intelligence. 2024.
source.label: Active intervention design in causal models

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: Publisher page metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: Store bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase; do not redistribute article text.

why_unverifiable: The project has not reproduced the external benchmarks or applied the method to a real MS-relevant perturbation experiment.
